adviceScreen.faoExplanation: Uses the simplified FAO-56 Single Crop Coefficient approach: Crop Water Need (ETc) = ET0 × Kc. Effective rain (80% of rain >= 5 mm) offsets depletion. When cumulative depletion reaches the allowed limit, irrigation is recommended.

savingsScreen.title: Water & Cost Savings
savingsScreen.subtitle: KhetiX Precision vs Traditional Flood Irrigation in Sindh
savingsScreen.calculatorSubtitle: Adjust your farm acres to project monthly water and tube-well diesel savings
savingsScreen.ruleOfThumbText: Traditional flood irrigation typically applies ~75 mm (~300,000 L/acre) per turn regardless of need. KhetiX recommends the exact crop requirement (35-45 mm), saving ~130,000 litres per acre per turn. Pumping 10,000 litres of groundwater consumes ~1.5 litres of diesel, yielding direct fuel savings of ~PKR 425 per 10k litres.

aboutScreen.title: About & Methodology
aboutScreen.subtitle: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith Atmospheric Water Balance
aboutScreen.missionText: KhetiX empowers smallholder farmers in Khairpur, Sindh, Pakistan to apply the 'Right water, at the right time'. By eliminating guesswork, farmers protect wheat and cotton yields from waterlogging and drought while slashing tube-well diesel expenses.
aboutScreen.pillar1Desc: Satellite and ground weather data (solar radiation, temperature, wind, humidity) from Open-Meteo.
aboutScreen.pillar2Desc: Calibrated crop water consumption coefficients across Initial, Development, Mid-Season, and Late-Season stages.
aboutScreen.pillar3Desc: Readily available water holding capacity for Sandy (25 mm), Loam (40 mm), and Clay (50 mm) soils of the Indus basin.
aboutScreen.pillar4Desc: Effective rain logic (80% of rainfall >= 5 mm) that postpones unnecessary irrigation when rain is expected.
aboutScreen.whyNoSensorsTitle: Why KhetiX Works Without Costly Hardware Sensors
aboutScreen.whyNoSensorsDesc: Physical IoT soil moisture probes cost Rs 50,000+, easily clog in Indus canal silt, and fail during power outages. KhetiX uses an atmospheric water-balance model (mass conservation) validated by the UN FAO. We calculate water leaving the field through evapotranspiration and water entering through rain or irrigation, delivering high accuracy at zero hardware cost to the farmer.
aboutScreen.refFao: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56: 'Crop Evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements' (Allen, Pereira, Raes, Smith).
aboutScreen.refMeteo: Open-Meteo High-Resolution Global Weather & Evapotranspiration Reanalysis API.
aboutScreen.refParc: Pakistan Agricultural Research Council (PARC) & Sindh Agriculture Extension guidelines for wheat and cotton cultivation.
aboutScreen.disclaimer: Disclaimer: KhetiX provides scientific decision support to optimize irrigation. Actual field conditions may vary based on salinity, drainage, and local canal rotation.
